name: Khakas

ancestors.notes: Descent from Proto-Turkic (South Siberian Turkic branch).
Russian adstrate: Soviet-era lexicon and long Siberian regional contact.

notes: Khakas (хакас тілі), a South Siberian Turkic language of the Republic of Khakassia, Russia, written in a Cyrillic alphabet reformed in 1939: the Russian letters plus ⟨ғ⟩ /ɣ/, ⟨і⟩ /ɘ/, ⟨ң⟩ /ŋ/, ⟨ӧ⟩ /ø/, ⟨ӱ⟩ /y/ and the affricate letter ⟨ӌ⟩ /dʒ/. Vowel length is phonemic and written by DOUBLING the vowel letter (аа ее ии оо ӧӧ уу ӱӱ ыы), listed as multigraph keys so maximal-munch matching prefers them over the single short-vowel letters. Vowel harmony (front/back, rounding) operates throughout. ⟨ф ц щ ъ ь⟩ occur mainly in Russian loanwords; the silent hard/soft signs carry no independent segment and are omitted from the grapheme map.
